name: Citizens Financial Group

reads.name: What they do
reads.evidence: Providence-based regional bank, $234.5B assets: takes deposits ($185.2B) and lends ($148.2B) to consumers, small businesses and mid-sized companies through 1,000+ branches in 14 states plus DC; also wealth, cards and a growing Private Bank.

reads.name: What they sell
reads.evidence: Q3 2026 revenue $2,322M: net interest income $1,675M (72%), fees $647M (28%: capital markets $149M, service charges $120M, wealth $109M record, card $90M, letters of credit/loan fees $54M, FX/derivatives $49M, mortgage $35M). FY2025 segments: Consumer Banking revenue $6,224M, Commercial Banking $2,773M.

reads.name: Who buys
reads.evidence: Diffuse. Loans $148.2B: commercial $77.2B (C&I $53.9B, 36% of loans, about 84% investment-grade equivalent; CRE $23.3B, 16%) and retail $71.0B. Leveraged loans only ~1.2% of loans. No single-customer concentration disclosed.

reads.name: Where they operate
reads.evidence: US only: 14 states and DC (New England, Mid-Atlantic, Midwest) plus national digital deposits, education and point-of-sale loans. No material FX exposure found (FX is client hedging fees, $49M). Regional concentration in the Northeast; NYC Metro and West Coast/Florida private-bank offices are expansions.

reads.name: Money model
reads.evidence: Spread bank: 72% of Q3 revenue from net interest (NIM 3.19%, total deposit cost 1.66%) and 28% from fees. Two sentences: it pays depositors less than it earns on loans and securities, and adds fees from wealth, capital markets and cards. Deposits stable at $185.2B (about 33% non-interest-bearing); loan-to-deposit 80.0%.

reads.name: Operations
reads.evidence: Efficiency ratio 60.0% (63.0% a year ago); positive operating leverage 5.3% YoY; expenses $1,393M flat QoQ; 17,609 FTEs. Bank costs are mostly people and fixed (operating leverage works both ways); capex not material. Reimagine the Bank targets ~$100M run-rate savings by YE2026, ~$225M YE2027, ~$450M+ YE2028 (about 50 of 50+ initiatives; 35+ launched). Guidance hit rate not formally tested: NIM rose 3.00% to 3.19% over four quarters, in line with the path shown.

reads.name: Supply chain
reads.evidence: Critical inputs are deposits (cost +3bp QoQ to 1.66%; Private Bank deposits $18.5B, +4% QoQ), wholesale funding (FHLB advances $7.6B vs $14M a year ago; long-term borrowings up $7.2B YoY) and regulatory capital. Suppliers: households/businesses (diffuse), FHLB, bond investors; no single point of failure, but funding mix has shifted to costlier wholesale. Passes costs on partly: slightly asset sensitive (~1% NII per 100bp gradual move), with receive-fixed swaps hedging lower rates through 2027. Signal tags: fed_funds, 2y (deposit cost), hy_spreads (wholesale issuance), real_spending (loan demand), regulation (AOCI/capital). Hike path raises deposit cost faster than fixed-rate assets reprice; spread widening raises debt cost.

reads.name: Edge
reads.evidence: Mid-size franchise without a dominant moat; edge is being built: Private Bank earns ROE >25% and added $0.16 of Q3 EPS (11%), revenue $188M vs $120M a year ago, client assets $12.4B, 12 advisor teams added since launch, 10 offices open and 6+ more planned 2027; plus NYC Metro, NExT deposit program, payments. Different right now: Private Bank buildout and terminating legacy swaps. The brief's 'hired from First Republic' detail was not verified in the filings read.

reads.name: Everyday brand
reads.evidence: Retail bank brand inside its 14-state footprint (1,000+ branches, 3,100 ATMs, ~$71B retail loans) but not a national everyday brand; customers would notice but could switch. Pricing power over rivals not evidenced; marketing spend per revenue dollar not found.

reads.name: Rivals and share
reads.evidence: 10-K peers: Comerica, Fifth Third, Huntington, KeyCorp, M&T, PNC, Regions, Truist, U.S. Bancorp. CFG loans +5% YoY and deposits +3% YoY, below the industry's ~7-9% loan and ~9.6% deposit growth (H.8). 2025 TSR 2nd among its regional peer group. Gaining share in Private Bank; losing in consumer deposits (Q3 consumer deposits down).

reads.name: Growth runway
reads.evidence: Private Bank loans $11.7B, up from $5.9B a year ago, and deposits $18.5B; Wealth fees +17% YoY; expansion offices planned 1H27-2H27; NIM guided to 3.30-3.50% by 4Q27 from 3.19%; Non-Core auto/education runoff down to ~$1.4B average from $3.3B a year ago frees capital for higher-return loans. Core loans +7% YoY. Much of this is already visible in results.

reads.name: Cash and leaders
reads.evidence: ROTCE 15.1% in Q3 (9-month 13.73%; FY2025 11.2%) vs ~10% cost of equity. Capital returned $322M in Q3 ($197M dividends, $125M buybacks at avg $70.76, now above the $61.76 price); dividend +13% to $0.52; new buyback capacity $1.95B (~$200M planned Q4); shares 431.5M to 421.2M (-2.4% YoY). CET1 10.5%. TBV/share $35.78, -2.6% YoY and -6.6% QoQ (AOCI -$3.37). Pay: PSUs score on ROTCE and EPS with a +/-20% relative-TSR modifier. Form 4 scan Aug-Nov 2026: only grants and tax withholding, no meaningful open-market buys (one 30-share purchase). Insider ownership % not extracted. Bank FCF not used.

reads.name: Durability
reads.evidence: Deposit-funded lending is not being displaced, and the bank is not losing relevance, but deposits are shifting to higher-cost products (savings -9% YoY, money market +6%), and wholesale funding is rising. Disruption/competition: larger banks, fintech, stablecoins (generic risk). Key-person: Chairman and CEO Van Saun, with a new CFO (Banerjee, Aug 2025) and new commercial head (Oct 2025). Rule-change risk: CET1 falls to 8.7% if AOCI opt-out is removed.

reads.name: Red flags
reads.evidence: Clean. 8-K Item 4.01 on 2026-10-30 is a planned auditor change (Deloitte to PwC, effective after the FY2026 audit) with no disagreements or reportable events and no adverse opinions; no 4.02; no NT filings; no CORRESP/UPLOAD letters since 2021 in the submissions list; Deloitte's FY2025 ICFR opinion unqualified; one critical audit matter (allowance for credit losses). 'Underlying' equals reported for 2025. Series G preferred redeemed Oct 6 2026. Watch: auditor change mid-transition.

reads.name: Regime fit
reads.evidence: Overheat: asset-sensitive (~1% NII per 100bp), NIM rising, but a hike lifts deposit costs (+3bp QoQ) and AOCI fell $3.37/share of TBV in Q3 as long yields rose (10y ~4.85-5.0%). Slowdown: credit-sensitive (NCOs 37bp, ACL 1.47%, lower than HBAN's 1.75%; CRE $23.3B, of which general office $1.9B at 7.6% reserve), but falling long yields would repair TBV and swaps hedge lower rates through 2027. Stagflation bad; boom good. Sensitive to rates, mildly to the dollar (none), input costs (funding).

reads.name: Rules and politics
reads.evidence: Standard bank supervision. Capital rules: CET1 10.5% reported but 8.7% if the AOCI opt-out were removed (about +60bp accretion expected by YE2028 as ~$1.1B of losses burn off). Q3 10-Q legal proceedings and any pending dockets not read in depth; no merger or other regulatory docket found.

reads.name: Price
reads.evidence: Price $61.76 (2026-11-25), TBV/share $35.78: P/TBV 1.73x. At 10% cost of equity and 3% growth that implies ROTCE ~15.1% (17.3% at 0% growth), equal to Q3 actual 15.1%, so the price already pays for today's recovered return. If the 16-18% target is met by end-2027, fair P/TBV is 1.86-2.14x ($66-77, +8% to +24% on today's TBV); at 13.9% (Q2 level) it is 1.56x ($56); at 12% it is 1.29x ($46). P/E 12.5x trailing EPS $4.96 (10.9x Q3 annualised $5.64). Own year-end P/TBV 2021-25 approx 1.14, 1.22, 0.98, 1.29, 1.49x (equity less preferred less goodwill; other intangibles ignored), so 1.73x is above the 5-year range; own year-end P/E 7.5-14.7x. Peers: HBAN 1.57x (ROTCE 14.6%), USB 2.00x (18.5%). Stock -11.7% since 8/26 but still +9% on the year.

status_reason: Quality B with a real ROTCE recovery (11.75% to 15.1% in four quarters, targets 16-18% by end-2027), but the price (1.73x TBV, above its own 5-year range) already pays for today's 15.1%, so there is no cushion and no clear market mistake.
answer_to_question: No: the ROTCE recovery is not under-priced. P/TBV 1.73x implies 15.1% ROTCE, exactly the Q3 actual; the market is already capitalising the recovery. Upside needs the 16-18% target delivered (swap drag nearly gone, NIM 3.30-3.50% by 4Q27, Reimagine savings): about +8% to +24% on today's TBV. Downside is larger if credit turns (12% ROTCE implies ~$46). Unlike Citi at 1.12x TBV, CFG is not priced on trough returns.
swap_repricing_schedule: Terminated-swap drag on NII per the Q3 deck (my reading of the chart): -$457M 2024, -$230M 2025, ~-$40M 2026, ~-$3M 2027: most of the tailwind is already in the numbers; remaining NIM lift to 3.30-3.50% comes from fixed-rate asset repricing and mix, with the deck's own range for the macro/balance-sheet component of -3 to +14bp.

feedback.fact: Total deposit costs +3bp QoQ to 1.66% and interest-bearing deposit costs +5bp to 2.13%; FHLB advances rose to $7.6B from $5.8B in one quarter; management assumes a 10-year Treasury ~5.00% through 2027 and calls the balance sheet slightly asset sensitive.
feedback.effect: confirms the Overheat hard-data read and the deposit-cost squeeze; also shows long yields (AOCI) hurt TBV (-6.6% QoQ)

feedback.fact: Credit 'broadly favorable': NCO 37bp stable, nonaccruals 0.99%, ACL 1.47%; CRE commercial loans -18% YoY in nonaccrual; but commercial loans -2% QoQ on CRE paydowns and lower line utilisation.
feedback.effect: no sign yet of the credit stress that HY spreads (3.72%, widening) imply; contradicts a Slowdown call in the bank's own book
